question: In a series LCR circuit connected to an AC voltage source, the voltage across the inductor ($V_L$) and the voltage across the capacitor ($V_C$) are both measured to be 200V, while the voltage across the resistor ($V_R$) is 100V. Why is the total source voltage not simply the algebraic sum $200 + 200 + 100 = 500V$?

options.A: Because AC voltmeters measure peak values, which cannot be added.
options.B: Because there is significant power loss in the connecting wires.
options.C: Because $V_L$ and $V_C$ are $180^\circ$ out of phase and cancel each other out.
options.D: Because the voltage across the inductor induces a back EMF that reduces the total.
